validity.researcher_notes: Sheet Operator is blank; Owner = 'Egyptian Natural Gas Holding Co [100.%]' (EGAS, the sector holding/asset company) on both the GGIT backend row and the operators/owners tab. Wiki lead claims Operator = 'Egyptian Natural Gas Company (GASCO)'. Verified independently (not via wiki): (1) Oil & Gas Journal, 'Egypt's natural gas future: A world class resource will fuel expanded local use and LNG exports' — states directly 'Gasco supplies gas to the Arab Natural Gas Pipeline and transmits natural gas to the Damietta LNG plant where it is exported to Europe,' i.e. GASCO is named as the transmission entity delivering gas to the Damietta/SEGAS LNG complex this pipeline feeds. (2) ICLG 'Oil & Gas Laws and Regulations Egypt' — independently corroborates the structural split: 'GASCO is a central operator across the national gas grid (transmission backbone and compressor stations)' while EGAS/holding companies sit at the upstream/coordination level — matching the sheet's Owner=EGAS pattern and explaining why Operator should be GASCO, not EGAS. Neither source is a wire-story duplicate of the other (trade journal vs. legal/regulatory guide, separate origins). OGJ is the only source naming Damietta/SEGAS specifically; ICLG confirms the general GASCO-operates/EGAS-owns structure that the sheet already reflects for Owner. This mirrors the row-specific attribution pattern flagged class-wide across Egypt gas trunk rows (P0477, P3346, P3366, etc.) in the 2026-07-13 operating deep sweep — GASCO is the transmission operator, EGAS the owner, and this row was simply missed. Could not find a source naming this exact 12 km Damietta–SEGAS spur (as opposed to the broader Damietta feed) and GASCO together, so tier is medium rather than high.
